source_title: Arcanum: Of Steamworks and Magick Obscura
continuity_scope: Original English Windows release (Troika Games/Sierra On-Line; 22 August 2001), witnessed through the Sierra-copyrighted English Arcanum Player's Guide preserved by SierraHelp. This excludes any patched, digital-store, modded, prototype, or particular player-campaign state.
work_or_witnesses: Arcanum: Of Steamworks and Magick Obscura, original English Windows release (22 August 2001)
Arcanum Player's Guide (English Sierra manual, 190-page archival scan)
Troika/Sierra Arcanum FAQ v1.0 (March 2000), archival copy
Steam product-support listing (later digital rerelease metadata)
coverage_rule: Include only fixed named dramatic NPCs directly identified and described in the selected Sierra manual's guided opening: Virgil, a human villager at the crash site who may optionally join, and Charles Brehgo, a cursed restless spirit who can offer an optional quest. Exclude the player character, including tutorial exemplar Merwin Tumblebrook; all other companion/NPC names require their own claim-level witness.
omissions: The player-created or selected protagonist, tutorial pre-fabricated Merwin Tumblebrook, and all player-specific backgrounds/alignment/choices are not nodes.
Other companions, antagonists, historical figures, factions, locations, and optional outcomes are omitted because this manual witness does not furnish a complete profile roster.

Patches (including later 1.0.7.4 references), Steam/GOG digital rereleases, unofficial restoration patches, mods, prototypes, multiplayer sessions, and player campaigns are separate version/continuity witnesses.
uncertainties: The Sierra manual is a historical scan hosted by an archival help site rather than a current Sierra/Activision endpoint; its copyright notice identifies Sierra On-Line, but scan provenance/page-to-disc concordance has not been independently verified.
Manual tutorial prose uses a selectable pre-fabricated character, Merwin, and a generic player character; neither establishes a fixed protagonist.
Virgil's party membership and Charles Brehgo's assistance are optional, so their records avoid any party, quest-resolution, alignment, or ending claim.

The manual's fictional racial treatise contains essentialist, prejudicial, colonial-science-style and derogatory in-world assertions. It is described only as a diegetic source voice, never mapped to real peoples or treated as factual taxonomy.
evidence_basis: Sierra-copyrighted English player-guide scan, archival Troika/Sierra FAQ, and official digital listing metadata. No fan wiki, Wikipedia, walkthrough, or mod documentation is used as character evidence.

citations.locator: Arcanum Player's Guide pp. 91-100; copyright pp. 182-186
supports: original manual identity, player/prototype boundary, Virgil, Charles Brehgo, followers, combat, and archival Sierra copyright statement
Troika/Sierra FAQ, magic/technology tension, industrial setting, player-story framing, and peoples/race tension
